She has worsening diffuse abdominal pain, a swollen abdomen, nausea and signs of peritoneal irritation. About 20 cm of small bowel, including diverticulum and perforation, was resected with side-to-side anastomosis, irrigation and drainage.

args.followup_or_handoff: No IV antibiotics were ordered or acknowledged during this encounter, so the receiving team must start them. For the surgical team: start IV broad-spectrum antibiotics for secondary peritonitis now. Give VTE prophylaxis. Resume or bridge anticoagulation for chronic AF once bleeding risk allows. Continue nasogastric decompression and IV fluids until bowel function returns. Run glucose checks with insulin as needed. Monitor heart rate for AF rate control. Give COPD bronchodilators and chest physiotherapy to prevent pulmonary complications. Watch the drain output and look for anastomotic leak or sepsis. Send the specimen for histopathology. Refer to gastroenterology/ERCP to review her biliary stent history and plan any needed biliary follow-up. Clarify her full medication list and allergies, which the source did not document. Escalate to ICU for hemodynamic instability, rising lactate or respiratory failure.
